package.name: llamaparse
package.packageFile:
$schema: ../_schema/package.schema.json

# LLAMAPARSE — document parsing whose OUTPUT IS MARKDOWN, which is the reason it exists alongside an
# element-array parser. An element array is the right shape for chunking and vector stores; an Agent
# prompt or a RAG context window usually wants one clean Markdown document, and LlamaParse's whole
# product is producing that well (tables as Markdown tables, reading order fixed, charts read on the
# top tier).
#
# THE v2 PARSE API (api.cloud.llamaindex.ai/api/v2/parse), which is a JOB: upload returns a receipt,
# status is polled, results are fetched with `expand`. Same capability set the unstructured package
# uses — multipart for the upload, poll for the wait, binary for fetching a document by url.

name: llamaparse
displayName: LlamaParse
description: Parse documents into clean Markdown and structured items with LlamaParse
version: 1.0.0
category: ingest
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1785840099/gravity/icons/lamaindex.png

features:
  - Parse PDF, Office and image documents into LLM-ready Markdown
  - Four cost/quality tiers, from fast to agentic chart-reading

# NO WILDCARD, deliberately. A url given to this node is handed to LlamaCloud as `source_url` and
# THEY fetch it — this node never dials the document's host at all, so the "*"-for-downloads idiom
# other document nodes need does not apply here.
#
# BOTH REGIONS, because a key belongs to exactly one and tells you only when the wrong host answers
# "Invalid API Key. Please check your region" (seen live 2026-08-04 — a US key, an EU console, and an
# activity page that swore nothing was happening). Declaring both means switching regions is ONLY the
# credential's API URL field; a self-hosted deployment's host still has to be added here.
allowedHosts:
  - api.cloud.llamaindex.ai
  - api.cloud.eu.llamaindex.ai

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.6.0"
  credential: [apiKeyHeader]
  transport: [json]
  # `multipart` only for the fileBase64 path — a url never uploads (see run.yaml).
  encoding: [multipart]
  # A parse is a JOB: without `poll` an executor would settle on the start receipt and emit it as
  # the answer, with nothing anywhere reporting a problem.
  poll: true

credentials.llamaCloudCredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

name: llamaCloudCredential
displayName: LlamaCloud
description: LlamaCloud API key for LlamaParse document parsing
documentationUrl: https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/general/api_key/

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your LlamaCloud API key (llx-...), from cloud.llamaindex.ai
  - name: apiUrl
    displayName: API URL
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: false
    # NOT cosmetic. LlamaCloud runs regional deployments — the EU region is
    # api.cloud.eu.llamaindex.ai and a key belongs to its region. Defaulting silently to the US host
    # would send documents to a region the account may not intend, and the request would fail with a
    # key error that points at the wrong cause.
    description: >-
      Override the API host, e.g. https://api.cloud.eu.llamaindex.ai for an EU-region account.
      Defaults to https://api.cloud.llamaindex.ai
    placeholder: https://api.cloud.llamaindex.ai

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector, in interface.yaml order.
#
# `response` is the LAST call's reply — the expanded results GET. Shapes are from the vendor's
# retrieving-results guide: `markdown_full`/`text_full` are single strings; `markdown`/`text`,
# `items` and `metadata` are `{ pages: [...] }`. The per-page fallbacks below matter on the `fast`
# tier, which supports no markdown at all — there `markdown` honestly emits ''.

- emit: markdown
  value: >-
    return response.markdown_full
      || (((response.markdown || {}).pages || []).map(p => p.markdown || '').join('\n\n'))

- emit: text
  value: >-
    return response.text_full
      || (((response.text || {}).pages || []).map(p => p.text || '').join('\n\n'))

- emit: items
  # Flattened across pages, so a consumer sees one list of typed elements (heading, table, ...)
  # each carrying its page_number. [] on the fast tier is the honest answer, not an error.
  value: >-
    return ((response.items || {}).pages || [])
      .map(p => (p.items || []).map(i => Object.assign({ page_number: p.page_number }, i)))
      .flat()

- emit: metadata
  # The job's own metadata plus the id, so a run can be traced in the LlamaCloud console.
  # pageCount from the metadata pages, which every tier returns.
  value: >-
    return (() => {
      const raw = calls.jobUrl || calls.jobUpload || {};
      const job = raw.job || raw;
      const pages = ((response.metadata || {}).pages || []);
      return { jobId: job.id || '',
               status: job.status || '',
               pageCount: pages.length,
               pages: pages,
               jobMetadata: response.job_metadata || {} };
    })();
files.api/run.yaml:
# THE v2 PARSE API, a JOB. Grounded in the vendor's REST reference and results guide
# (developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/parse/guides/api-reference/ + retrieving-results/, 2026-08-04):
#   POST /api/v2/parse               JSON { source_url | file_id, tier, version, page_ranges? }
#   POST /api/v2/parse/upload        multipart `file` + `configuration` (a JSON text field)
#   GET  /api/v2/parse/{job_id}      status: PENDING | RUNNING | COMPLETED | FAILED | CANCELLED
#   GET  /api/v2/parse/{job_id}?expand=...   the results
#
# TWO WAYS IN, chosen by which input the box holds, and the difference is not style:
#
#   A URL becomes `source_url` and LLAMACLOUD fetches the document itself. The first build
#   downloaded the url here and re-uploaded it as multipart — which put a 13MB document through the
#   author's uplink at ~230KB/s, a minute of sending that the vendor's edge sometimes killed with a
#   499 mid-body. `source_url` moves that transfer onto the vendor's own network and deletes this
#   node's download call entirely.
#
#   Bytes in hand (fileBase64) still have to travel, so the upload endpoint stays for exactly that
#   case, with the patience the slow path taught: a five-minute window and retries on the edge's
#   give-up statuses.
#
# THE HOST COMES FROM THE CREDENTIAL: LlamaCloud is regional (the EU host is
# api.cloud.eu.llamaindex.ai) and a key belongs to its region. The default below is the US host, and
# any other must also be added to package.yaml allowedHosts.

# START FROM A URL. `when` — exactly one of the two starts runs, and a skipped call leaves no trace.
- name: jobUrl
  when: "return !!String(config.fileUrl || '').trim() && !config.fileBase64"
  method: POST
  url: >-
    return (credentials.llamaCloudCredential.apiUrl || 'https://api.cloud.llamaindex.ai')
      .replace(/\/+$/, '') + '/api/v2/parse'

  credential:
    scheme: apiKeyHeader
    header: Authorization
    value: "return 'Bearer ' + credentials.llamaCloudCredential.apiKey"

  body:
    source_url: "{{ config.fileUrl }}"
    tier: "return config.tier || 'cost_effective'"
    # `latest` rather than a pinned date, because a manifest cannot be re-released every time the
    # vendor ships.
    version: latest
    # Omitted when blank, which is "whole document" without saying so.
    page_ranges: "return String(config.pageRanges || '').trim() || undefined"

  transport: json
  timeoutMs: 120000

  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]

  # LlamaCloud reports refusal in `detail` (FastAPI convention), judged by shape rather than status.
  error:
    when: "return !!response.detail"
    message: >-
      return typeof response.detail === 'string' ? response.detail : JSON.stringify(response.detail)

  # An agentic parse of a long document is slow — minutes, not seconds. 5s × 300 attempts is 25
  # minutes of patience, under the platform's own 300-poll ceiling.
  # THE STATUS REPLY IS WRAPPED AND THE START REPLY IS NOT — seen live, not documented. POST
  # /api/v2/parse answers { id, status } flat, while GET /api/v2/parse/{id} answers { job: { id,
  # status }, text, markdown, ... }. `(response.job || response)` reads both, and without it the
  # poll watched a status field that never existed and the first run only LOOKED stuck — the new
  # poll logs said "(no status field)" on the first heartbeat, which is exactly this.
  poll:
    until: "return (response.job || response).status === 'COMPLETED'"
    failed: "return ['FAILED', 'CANCELLED'].indexOf((response.job || response).status) !== -1"
    message: "return (() => { const j = response.job || response; return 'LlamaParse job ' + (j.id || '') + ' ended ' + j.status + (j.error_message ? ': ' + j.error_message : ''); })()"
    url: >-
      return (credentials.llamaCloudCredential.apiUrl || 'https://api.cloud.llamaindex.ai')
        .replace(/\/+$/, '') + '/api/v2/parse/' + response.id
    intervalMs: 5000
    maxAttempts: 300

# START FROM BYTES — the document is already in hand as base64, so it has no url to give and must be
# uploaded. One receipt shape either way: what this call's name holds is the FINISHED job's status
# payload, same as jobUrl's.
- name: jobUpload
  when: "return !!config.fileBase64"
  method: POST
  url: >-
    return (credentials.llamaCloudCredential.apiUrl || 'https://api.cloud.llamaindex.ai')
      .replace(/\/+$/, '') + '/api/v2/parse/upload'

  credential:
    scheme: apiKeyHeader
    header: Authorization
    value: "return 'Bearer ' + credentials.llamaCloudCredential.apiKey"

  encoding: multipart

  body:
    # THE FILE PART. `{ base64, mimeType, filename }` is the shape the executor turns back into
    # bytes. The FILENAME matters more than it looks: the parser picks its reader from the
    # extension, which is why `fileName` is a first-class config field rather than a constant.
    file: >-
      return { base64: config.fileBase64,
               mimeType: 'application/octet-stream',
               filename: config.fileName || 'document.pdf' };

    # THE CONFIGURATION, a JSON text field (a non-file object part is stringified by the executor).
    configuration: >-
      return { tier: config.tier || 'cost_effective',
               version: 'latest',
               page_ranges: String(config.pageRanges || '').trim() || undefined };

  transport: json
  # FIVE MINUTES, most of which is the BODY leaving: a large document on a slow uplink takes a
  # minute or more just to send, and the edge then thinks before it answers. 120s was tight enough
  # to look like a vendor error.
  timeoutMs: 300000

  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    # 499 and 408 are the edge giving up on a SLOW UPLOAD, seen live on a document that succeeded
    # on retry — transient by demonstration, so they retry with the server errors.
    on: [408, 429, 499, 500, 502, 503, 504]

  error:
    when: "return !!response.detail"
    message: >-
      return typeof response.detail === 'string' ? response.detail : JSON.stringify(response.detail)

  # THE STATUS REPLY IS WRAPPED AND THE START REPLY IS NOT — seen live, not documented. POST
  # /api/v2/parse answers { id, status } flat, while GET /api/v2/parse/{id} answers { job: { id,
  # status }, text, markdown, ... }. `(response.job || response)` reads both, and without it the
  # poll watched a status field that never existed and the first run only LOOKED stuck — the new
  # poll logs said "(no status field)" on the first heartbeat, which is exactly this.
  poll:
    until: "return (response.job || response).status === 'COMPLETED'"
    failed: "return ['FAILED', 'CANCELLED'].indexOf((response.job || response).status) !== -1"
    message: "return (() => { const j = response.job || response; return 'LlamaParse job ' + (j.id || '') + ' ended ' + j.status + (j.error_message ? ': ' + j.error_message : ''); })()"
    url: >-
      return (credentials.llamaCloudCredential.apiUrl || 'https://api.cloud.llamaindex.ai')
        .replace(/\/+$/, '') + '/api/v2/parse/' + response.id
    intervalMs: 5000
    maxAttempts: 300

# THE RESULTS, the same status GET with `expand` — a separate call rather than expand on every poll,
# because a full document in every status check is weight the wait does not need.
#
# `markdown_full`/`text_full` are the CONCATENATED strings (retrieving-results guide); `items` and
# `metadata` come back as { pages: [...] }. The `fast` tier DOES NOT SUPPORT MARKDOWN — asking for a
# markdown field on it is a validation error, not an empty answer — so the expand list is built from
# the tier rather than written once.
- name: result
  method: GET
  url: >-
    return (credentials.llamaCloudCredential.apiUrl || 'https://api.cloud.llamaindex.ai')
      .replace(/\/+$/, '') + '/api/v2/parse/'
      + (() => { const r = calls.jobUrl || calls.jobUpload || {}; return (r.job || r).id; })()
      + '?expand=' + (config.tier === 'fast'
          ? 'text_full,items,metadata,job_metadata'
          : 'markdown_full,text_full,items,metadata,job_metadata')

  credential:
    scheme: apiKeyHeader
    header: Authorization
    value: "return 'Bearer ' + credentials.llamaCloudCredential.apiKey"

  transport: json
  timeoutMs: 120000

  error:
    when: "return !!response.detail"
    message: >-
      return typeof response.detail === 'string' ? response.detail : JSON.stringify(response.detail)
files.config.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [tier]
  properties:
    fileUrl:
      type: string
      title: File URL
      description: >-
        A URL to fetch the document from. Use this OR File (base64). Usually wired from an upstream
        node, e.g. return signal.s3files1.files[0].downloadUrl
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    fileBase64:
      type: string
      title: File (base64)
      description: The document itself, base64 encoded, when it is not reachable by URL.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    fileName:
      type: string
      title: File Name
      description: >-
        Name including extension, e.g. report.pdf. The parser picks its reader from this, so a wrong
        or missing extension is the commonest cause of a poor parse.
      default: document.pdf
      "ui:field": template
    tier:
      type: string
      title: Tier
      # REQUIRED, because it is the COST dial as much as the quality one: `fast` is the cheapest path
      # and `agentic_plus` runs chart reading on every page at a multiple of the price. Left unset the
      # vendor picks, which is how a large batch quietly becomes expensive. It has a default, so
      # requiring it costs an author nothing — it just makes the choice visible.
      description: >-
        How hard to work. `fast` is cheapest but produces plain text ONLY — no markdown, no items.
        `cost_effective` balances price and quality. `agentic` handles hard layouts. `agentic_plus`
        also reads charts.
      enum: [fast, cost_effective, agentic, agentic_plus]
      enumNames:
        - Fast (cheapest, text only)
        - Cost effective (balanced)
        - Agentic (hard layouts)
        - Agentic plus (also reads charts)
      default: cost_effective
    pageRanges:
      type: string
      title: Page Ranges
      description: >-
        Only parse these pages, e.g. 1-3,7. Leave blank for the whole document. Fewer pages is
        directly less cost on every tier.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template

    # WHO MAY RUN THIS BOX, set by whoever builds the workflow (15-who-can-run-it.md).
    #
    # INSTANCE config, not the manifest's `auth`: the manifest is the node author's FLOOR, these are
    # the builder's per box, because the same node type legitimately faces staff on one workflow and
    # customers on another. The executor takes the STRICTER of the two.
    authRequired:
      type: boolean
      title: Require sign-in
      description: Only signed-in callers can run this step.
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
    authRole:
      type: string
      title: Require role
      description: A claim the caller must carry, like finance:approve.
      default: ""
      "ui:dependencies": { authRequired: true }

"ui:order":
  [authRequired, authRole, fileUrl, fileBase64, fileName, tier, pageRanges]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: file
    type: object
    description: "The document: { downloadUrl } or { content } base64, as S3 Files and Cloudinary emit"
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: markdown
    type: string
    description: The whole document as one Markdown string, tables rendered as Markdown tables
  - name: text
    type: string
    description: The whole document as plain text
  - name: items
    type: array
    description: Structured layout items — headings, paragraphs, tables — with type and content
  - name: metadata
    type: object
    description: jobId, pageCount and the job's own metadata, for tracing and billing

credentials:
  - name: llamaCloudCredential
    required: true
files.node.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/node.schema.json

type: LlamaParse
kind: PromiseNode

name: LlamaParse
category: Documents
color: "#8B5CF6"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1785840099/gravity/icons/lamaindex.png

description: Parse any document into clean, LLM-ready Markdown with LlamaParse. PDF, Word, slides, spreadsheets, images.

# Outcome first, then disqualify by PROPERTY. Doc 14: never name another node — the property that
# distinguishes this parser is its OUTPUT SHAPE (one Markdown document, tables as Markdown tables),
# so the meta says that rather than comparing.
whenToUse: >-
  Turn an existing document into clean Markdown an Agent can read directly: a PDF, Word file, slides,
  spreadsheet, scanned page or a photo of one. Best when the consumer is a prompt or a RAG context —
  it fixes reading order and renders tables as Markdown tables, and the top tiers read charts and
  complex layouts. It only READS a file that already exists, so it cannot author or revise one, and
  its output is a document, not a database of elements.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node. `required: false` adds no
# requirement of its own: the trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and
# requirements only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # Parsing IS deterministic for a given file, so cache BY CONTENT IDENTITY, never by URL.
  # `fileUrl` is usually a presigned link: a new signature every run over the same bytes, so
  # it is transport, not identity — `ignore` drops it from the fingerprint. The identity is
  # the `etag` an upstream file node (S3FileContent) delivers with the file. When no etag
  # arrives (a bare hand-typed URL), the key collects nothing and the run is NOT cached —
  # which keeps the old caution: a stale transcript of the wrong document is worse than
  # parsing twice.
  cacheable:
    ignore: [fileUrl]
    key: [etag]
files.test.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/test.schema.json

# Running it live needs LLAMACLOUD_API_KEY. It reaches the real API and bills per page, so the fixture
# uses a ONE-PAGE public PDF and the cheapest tier — still proving the whole chain: the url becomes a
# `source_url` job (LlamaCloud fetches it, nothing is uploaded), the job is polled to COMPLETED and
# the expanded results come back.
#
# `tier: fast` deliberately, both as the cheap path and because it is the tier that produces NO
# markdown and NO items — so those assertions below are about SHAPE ('' and [] are correct), and the
# CONTENT assertion rides on `text`, which every tier returns.

testData:
  config:
    fileUrl: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ER/tests/xhtml/testfiles/resources/pdf/dummy.pdf
    fileName: dummy.pdf
    tier: fast
  inputs:
    file:
      downloadUrl: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ER/tests/xhtml/testfiles/resources/pdf/dummy.pdf
  expect:
    # REAL CONTENT, not merely a string: an empty parse would still be "" and has to read as failure.
    text: "return typeof output.text === 'string' && output.text.length > 0"
    markdown: "return typeof output.markdown === 'string'"
    items: "return Array.isArray(output.items)"
    metadata: "return typeof output.metadata.jobId === 'string' && output.metadata.jobId.length > 0"
